hens_rule_text: Up to 6 hens allowed per single-family dwelling with no permit needed, if setback and coop standards are met.
permit_notes: No permit needed when the dwelling setback, side-yard setback, coop and sanitation rules are all met. A permit (with a variance explanation) is required if a resident cannot meet one of those standards.
setback_notes: 25 ft setback from dwellings and a separate 5 ft side-yard setback apply to the coop and enclosure.
coop_rules: Covered, predator-proof, well-ventilated coop with at least 1 sq ft per hen, plus a fenced outdoor enclosure; coop and enclosure kept sanitary and free of offensive odor.
hoa_note: Homeowners associations, deed restrictions and leases can be stricter than city law. Check yours before getting chickens.

sources.name: City of Toledo, Keeping Chickens (official page)

research_notes: Facts come from a search-result extract of the city's own official Keeping Chickens page; the full page text was not opened directly from this machine. No 2023 to 2026 amendment was found. Ohio has no known state law overriding this.
